title: Independence of coordinates under the uniform law
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, and equip the finite set of functions $x\colon \{0,1,\dots,n-1\} \to \{\text{neither},\text{leftOnly},\text{rightOnly}\}$ with the uniform probability law (each of the $3^n$ such functions is equally likely). Then the coordinate maps $x \mapsto x(i)$, for $i = 0,1,\dots,n-1$, are mutually independent random variables.
hypotheses_covered: n is a positive natural number
the law is uniform on all functions Fin n → DisjointCoordinate (three-valued type)
the family indexed by i of coordinate projections
replaced: Under the uniform disjoint-coordinate-vector law, the coordinates are independent.
